learn.title: Network security and load balancing/routing design
objectives: Layer network controls: NSGs and application security groups, Azure Firewall (Basic, Standard, Premium) with Firewall Manager policies, forced tunnelling and hub-and-spoke segmentation
Protect web and public endpoints with Web Application Firewall on Application Gateway or Front Door and with DDoS IP Protection or DDoS Network Protection

Secure administrative access and PaaS access with Azure Bastion, just-in-time VM access, private endpoints and disabled public network access, and enforce org-wide rules with Azure Virtual Network Manager security admin rules
Choose a load balancer with the Azure decision tree: global vs regional and HTTP(S) vs non-HTTP(S) across Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door and Traffic Manager
Design routing: Traffic Manager routing methods and nested profiles, Front Door origin groups and rules, Application Gateway listeners and rules, and Load Balancer regional and global tiers
concepts: NSG and application security group

An NSG filters traffic at Layer 3/4 on a subnet or NIC with priority-ordered allow and deny rules, service tags and default rules. An application security group groups NICs (all in the same VNet) so rules can target workloads instead of IP addresses.
Azure Firewall SKUs

Basic (up to 250 Mbps, threat intelligence alert only) for small environments; Standard (up to 30 Gbps) adds DNS proxy, web categories and threat-intelligence deny; Premium (up to 100 Gbps) adds outbound TLS inspection, IDPS and full URL filtering.
Firewall policy and Firewall Manager

A firewall policy is a reusable resource that works across regions and subscriptions. A child policy inherits the parent's rule collections, which are processed first; NAT rules aren't inherited, and the child can only make threat intelligence stricter. Parent and child must be in the same region.
Forced tunnelling
Routing Azure Firewall's internet-bound traffic to an on-premises or NVA next hop. It needs the Firewall Management NIC, and DNAT isn't supported in that mode because of asymmetric routing.
Web Application Firewall

Protects HTTP(S) apps against OWASP attacks with managed and custom rules (rate limits, geo-filtering). It runs regionally on Application Gateway WAF v2 or globally at the edge on Front Door; Front Door managed rule sets and bot protection need Premium. Start in Detection mode, then switch to Prevention.
DDoS protection tiers

Infrastructure protection is free and always on. DDoS IP Protection is billed per protected public IP. DDoS Network Protection covers VNets through a plan and adds rapid response support, cost protection and a WAF discount. Public IPs on a NAT gateway aren't protected.
Azure Bastion SKUs

Developer is free, shared and one VM at a time with no peering. Basic is dedicated with fixed capacity. Standard adds native client, file transfer, shareable links, IP-based connect and host scaling. Premium adds session recording and private-only deployment.
Just-in-time VM access

A Defender for Servers Plan 2 feature that keeps management ports closed through NSG or Azure Firewall rules and opens them for an approved IP for a limited time. It doesn't support firewalls managed by Firewall Manager policies.
Security admin rules

Azure Virtual Network Manager rules applied to network groups of VNets and evaluated before NSGs. Allow passes traffic on to NSGs; Deny and Always Allow end evaluation, so NSGs can't override them. They don't apply to subnets holding services such as Azure Firewall, Bastion or VPN Gateway.
Load-balancing decision tree

Ask: is it HTTP(S)? Is it internet-facing? Is it global or multi-region? Is acceleration needed? Is per-request L7 processing needed inside the region? The answers lead to Load Balancer, Application Gateway, Front Door, or Front Door combined with Application Gateway or Load Balancer.
Traffic Manager routing methods

DNS-based global routing with six methods: Priority (failover), Weighted (split or migrate), Performance (lowest latency), Geographic (sovereignty), Multivalue (all healthy IPs) and Subnet (by source IP range). Nested profiles combine methods.
Global Load Balancer

The global (cross-region) tier of Standard Load Balancer: a Layer 4 pass-through service with a static anycast public IP that fronts public regional load balancers, preserves client IP and fails over without DNS changes. It has no outbound rules and no internal frontend.
comparisons: Front Door is a global Layer 7 reverse proxy with caching, WAF and fast failover for HTTP(S). Traffic Manager only answers DNS, so it works for any protocol and external endpoints, but failover depends on DNS caching.

Application Gateway is a regional terminating proxy with TLS offload, path and host routing, rewrites, cookie affinity and WAF. Load Balancer is a pass-through Layer 4 service for any TCP or UDP traffic with ultra-low latency, HA ports and source IP affinity.

NSGs are free, distributed Layer 3/4 filters on subnets and NICs. Azure Firewall is a central, stateful service with FQDN and application rules, threat intelligence, logging and, in Premium, TLS inspection and IDPS. Use both together.
DDoS IP Protection vs Network Protection
IP Protection suits a few public IPs and is billed per IP. Network Protection is priced per 100 protected IP addresses and adds rapid response, cost protection and WAF discounts.
WAF on Application Gateway vs Front Door
Application Gateway WAF protects regional apps, including private-only ones. Front Door WAF blocks attacks at the global edge before they reach any region and suits multi-region public apps.
Standard gives caching, routing, rules engine and custom WAF rules. Premium adds Microsoft-managed WAF rule sets, bot protection, Private Link origins and the WAF report.
traps: Front Door, Application Gateway and WAF are HTTP(S) only; for UDP or other non-HTTP traffic across regions, use global Load Balancer or Traffic Manager.
Azure Firewall Premium inspects outbound TLS; inbound TLS termination is done by Application Gateway in front of the firewall.
Standard Load Balancer and Standard public IPs block inbound traffic until an NSG allows it.
Traffic Manager geographic routing returns NODATA for unmapped regions; map 'World' to a nested profile.
Security admin Allow rules still let NSGs deny traffic; use Always Allow to guarantee access.
Bastion Developer doesn't support peered VNets, and only Premium records sessions or runs without a public IP.
revision: Pick the lowest Azure Firewall SKU that meets the need: Basic for small sites, Standard for web categories and DNS proxy, Premium for TLS inspection, IDPS and URL paths.
Use Firewall Manager parent and child policies for central rules with local additions.
Send spoke-to-spoke and internet traffic through the hub firewall with UDRs, or use secured virtual hubs with routing intent in Virtual WAN.
Disable public network access on PaaS services and reach them through private endpoints; enable private endpoint network policies to apply NSGs.
Global HTTP(S) app: Front Door. Regional HTTP(S) app: Application Gateway. Regional non-HTTP: Load Balancer. Global non-HTTP: global Load Balancer or Traffic Manager.
Add Application Gateway behind Front Door only when each region needs in-VNet L7 processing; add Load Balancer behind Front Door for IaaS VMs.
Choose Traffic Manager methods by goal: Priority for failover, Weighted for migration, Performance for latency, Geographic for sovereignty, Subnet for IP ranges, Multivalue for client retries.
Lock origins to your Front Door with the AzureFrontDoor.Backend tag plus the X-Azure-FDID header, or use Premium Private Link origins.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A three-tier application runs on VMs in one subnet. VMs scale in and out often, so their IP addresses change. The security team wants rules such as 'web tier may reach app tier on 8080' without maintaining IP lists. What should you recommend?
opts: Service endpoints enabled for each tier
Azure Firewall IP Groups updated by a script
A separate route table for each tier
Application security groups referenced in NSG rules
questions.e: Application security groups let NSG rules target a logical group of NICs instead of explicit IP addresses.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A small company needs a managed, stateful Azure firewall for a single VNet with about 100 Mbps of traffic. It needs network and application rules with SNAT/DNAT but no web categories, DNS proxy or TLS inspection, and must minimise cost. Which Azure Firewall SKU should you recommend?
opts: Azure Firewall Standard
Azure Firewall Premium
Azure Firewall Basic
A third-party NVA in a scale set
questions.e: Basic is the lowest-cost SKU, supports up to 250 Mbps and provides core L3-L7 filtering.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A payment processor must decrypt and inspect outbound HTTPS traffic from its Azure workloads and detect known attack signatures in that traffic. Which solution should you recommend?
opts: Application Gateway WAF v2 in prevention mode
NSG flow analysis with Microsoft Sentinel rules
Azure Firewall Standard with threat intelligence in deny mode
Azure Firewall Premium with TLS inspection and IDPS

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: Developers may browse https://contoso-docs.example.com/public/ but must be blocked from https://contoso-docs.example.com/admin/ on the same host. The company uses Azure Firewall for outbound traffic. Which capability is required?
opts: Application rules with FQDN filtering in Standard
URL filtering in Azure Firewall Premium
Network rules with FQDN filtering on all ports
Web categories in Azure Firewall Standard
questions.e: FQDN filtering only sees the host name. Filtering on the full path needs TLS termination, which is a Premium feature.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A school wants to block outbound access from its Azure virtual desktops to gambling and social networking sites by category. It doesn't need TLS inspection or IDPS and wants to minimise cost. Which Azure Firewall SKU should you recommend?
opts: Azure Firewall Premium
Azure Firewall Basic with threat intelligence
Azure Firewall Standard
Azure Firewall Basic

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: An architect plans to use FQDNs in Azure Firewall network rules so that SQL traffic on port 1433 to a partner's host name is allowed. Clients resolve names with their own DNS servers. Why could this design fail, and what fixes it?
opts: The firewall and clients may resolve different IPs; enable DNS proxy and point clients to the firewall
Network rules accept only IP addresses; move the rule to a DNAT collection
Port 1433 is blocked by default; add an NSG rule on AzureFirewallSubnet
FQDN network rules need Premium; upgrade the firewall to Premium
questions.e: FQDN filtering in network rules relies on the firewall's own DNS resolution, so clients should use the firewall as DNS proxy to stay consistent.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A company has Azure Firewall instances in hub VNets in six regions. A central team must define baseline rules once, while regional teams add local rules without changing the baseline. Administrative effort must be minimal. What should you recommend?
opts: One policy per region copied from a template spec each month
Azure Virtual Network Manager connectivity configurations per region
Classic rules exported and imported to each firewall by script
A parent firewall policy inherited by regional child policies in Azure Firewall Manager

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A child Azure Firewall policy inherits from a parent policy. Which statements are true? 1) Network rule collections from the parent are processed before the child's network rule collections. 2) NAT rule collections are inherited from the parent. 3) Network rule collections are processed before application rule collections. 4) The child can switch threat intelligence from 'Alert and deny' to 'Off'.
opts: Statements 1, 2 and 3 only
Statements 1, 3 and 4 only
Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 2 and 4 only
questions.e: NAT rules aren't inherited, and a child can only make threat intelligence stricter.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: Regulations require that all internet-bound traffic from Azure passes through the on-premises edge firewall after Azure Firewall inspects it. The data path must not use a public IP. How should you deploy Azure Firewall?
opts: With the Firewall Management NIC enabled and a default route on AzureFirewallSubnet to on-premises
With DNAT rules that send traffic to the on-premises firewall
With threat intelligence in deny mode and no public IP at all
With a UDR of 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet on AzureFirewallSubnet
questions.e: Forced tunnelling requires the Management NIC, whose public IP is used only by the platform, so the data path can be private.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A public web application runs in three Azure regions behind a global entry point. The company wants OWASP managed rules and bot protection enforced at the edge, before traffic reaches any region. What should you recommend?

Azure Web Application Firewall on Front Door Standard

Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door Premium

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: A storage account holds sensitive data. Only VMs in an Azure VNet and on-premises clients over ExpressRoute private peering may access it; the internet must be blocked entirely. What should you recommend?

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security
questions.q: In a hub-and-spoke network, traffic between spoke VNets must be inspected by Azure Firewall in the hub. Spokes are peered only to the hub. What should you recommend?
opts: Direct peering between spokes with gateway transit
Service endpoints on every spoke subnet
NSGs in each spoke that allow only hub addresses

questions.e: Peering isn't transitive, so spokes reach each other only through the hub when UDRs point at the firewall.

questions.on: Recommend a solution to optimize network security

questions.q: A game studio runs UDP game servers behind Standard Load Balancers in four regions. Players need one static anycast IP, routing to the closest healthy region, preservation of the client IP and failover that doesn't wait on DNS caches. What should you recommend?
opts: Application Gateway with backends in every region
Azure Front Door Premium
Azure Traffic Manager with performance routing
A global (cross-region) Azure Load Balancer

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution

opts: Geographic
Performance
Priority

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution
questions.q: A Traffic Manager profile uses geographic routing with endpoints mapped to Europe and North America. Users in Brazil report the name doesn't resolve. What should you recommend?
opts: Lower the DNS TTL on the profile
Switch the profile to Multivalue routing
Enable endpoint monitoring on the Europe endpoint
Map 'World' to a nested endpoint that has at least two endpoints
questions.e: Queries from unmapped regions get a NODATA response, so Microsoft recommends a World mapping, ideally to a nested profile.

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution
questions.q: A company wants employees connecting from the head office's public IP range to reach a preview deployment, while everyone else reaches production, using the same DNS name. Which Traffic Manager routing method should you use?
opts: Weighted
Performance
Subnet

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution
questions.q: Users must reach the lowest-latency region, and within the West Europe region traffic must be split 80/20 between two deployments for a canary test. What should you recommend?
opts: A parent performance profile with a nested weighted profile for West Europe
A geographic profile with a nested priority profile
A single weighted profile with region-specific weights
A single performance profile with two West Europe endpoints
questions.e: A profile has one routing method; nesting combines methods.

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution
questions.q: A global HTTPS app uses Traffic Manager priority routing. During a regional outage, some users kept hitting the failed region for several minutes even after Traffic Manager marked it degraded. What should you recommend to reduce failover time?
opts: Switch Traffic Manager to weighted routing
Add a second Traffic Manager profile as backup
Replace Traffic Manager with Azure Front Door
Deploy Application Gateway in the secondary region
questions.e: Traffic Manager works through DNS, so client and resolver caches delay failover; Front Door fails over at the proxy layer.

questions.on: Recommend a load-balancing and routing solution

A Traffic Manager profile per website
